findings.issue: The guard is correct, but if the card keeps declining it creates a dead end with no documented exit. Once a sibling holds the shipping, the FAILED shipment can only leave the state through a successful cancel retry: the reclaim bumps the attempt, re-freezes as a remainder with no shipping, and the card is retried under `-r<n>`. The cancel route is fixed to refundTo=SOURCE, so if payment-service keeps reporting FAILED (card closed, gateway refusal), the shipment can be neither shipped (409) nor cancelled (503). It is not blocked forever in the normal case, because any accepted retry finishes it. There is just no escape hatch and no runbook entry for the persistent-decline case.
findings.fix: Part B/B3 runbook: document that the guard 409 is cleared by retrying the cancel, give the query for FAILED shipments whose siblings carry `cancel_shipping_refund > 0`, and add a backlog item for an admin 'refund to wallet' option on the cancel (route PAYMENT_WALLET) for persistent card declines. No code change is needed for this PR.

summary: The AC-7 major is closed at 0727afe. `Order.advanceShipment` now refuses with 409 to ship a shipment with a FAILED claim while another shipment holds a live claim (REQUESTED or DONE) with `cancel_shipping_refund > 0`. That covers both remaining orderings: (a) a whole cancel stopped at S2 FAILED with S3 REQUESTED-completing, tested by `failedClaim_siblingHoldsShipping_shipIsRefused`, and (b) S1 REQUESTED, then S2 completing DONE, then S1 FAILED, tested by `siblingDoneWithShipping_thenFailed_shipIsRefused`. The guard is precise. A sibling can only have frozen as completing with shipping if the FAILED shipment was counted as covered at that moment. A pre-dispatch shipment has no returns, and FAILED claims no longer count as covered, so the guard never blocks a ship the money did not depend on. It also does not block a legitimate ship forever. A retry of the cancel reclaims under the next key, re-freezes as the remainder with no shipping (shipping is already taken), and commits on any accepted card refund. Only a card that is permanently declined leaves the shipment stuck. That case belongs in the runbook and a backlog item (minor), not this PR. The round-2 analysis still holds: a re-frozen claim never double-counts against a sibling, and keys never carry two amounts. Line count (586) is under the 600 ceiling. The approval assumes the CEO records V-ALL and forge-verify for this SHA before the gate, as stated, and assumes Part B merges with A (CTO condition 1).
